title: Grateful Dead Live at The Warehouse on 1970-02-01
lineage: SBD > MSR > C > DAT > CD > EAC > shntool > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with a Bob‑Weir‑heavy early mix, but a thrilling set highlighted by an epic The Other One → Lovelight pairing and tight China Cat Sunflower→I Know You Rider flow.
ai_review.review: The SBD capture is uneven – Bob Weir sits too high in the mix at the start, burying drums and other instruments – yet it settles after the Bear solo and becomes quite listenable. Musically the show shines with a massive Lovelight, a powerful The Other One, and tight transitions from China Cat Sunflower into I Know You Rider, making it a solid 1970 performance despite a few cuts and occasional raggedness.

ai_rating.rationale: All ten reviews are 4‑star or higher, praising the show’s jams while noting consistent mix issues; the strong musical highlights outweigh the technical flaws.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early part of the set is dominated by Bob Weir in the right channel, making drums and other instruments hard to hear; mix improves after the Bear solo with more balanced levels. Overall clarity is acceptable but inconsistent.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert opens with a quirky beat‑count debate and an unbalanced mix, but settles into a smooth flow after the first few songs. Highlights include the seamless China Cat → I Know You Rider transition and the marathon The Other One → Lovelight finale, giving the show both high‑energy peaks and relaxed moments.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar is clear later in the set (especially on Cold Rain) and audible during China Cat; early mix muffles him but improves.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass becomes more present after the mix settles, notably during I Know You Rider's a‑cappella ending.
band_member_comments.Bob: Dominates the right channel throughout, especially early; fans of his playing will love the prominence despite balance issues.
band_member_comments.Drums: Generally low in the mix and at times inaudible early on; described as long‑winded but recovers later.
